title: It Was Launched Last Year -- The Language of the Announcement
desc: The passive voice, and what it hides when a company writes about itself. Key expressions: to implement, rollout, to be staffed, statement, to revise, to issue, to be affected, pending, as of, to notify, in stages, mandatory. Structure: be plus the third form -- present, past, present perfect and future -- and when the passive is the right choice.
vocab: To implement
to put a decision or a plan into practice
The new structure will be implemented in stages.
Rollout
the gradual introduction of a new system across a company
The rollout of the booking platform starts in March.
To be staffed
to have all the positions in a team filled
The Bogota office has been fully staffed since last week.
Statement
an official written position on something
A statement was issued to all four countries on Monday.
To revise
to change a document or a price after reviewing it
The corporate fare structure has been revised.
To issue
to send out an official document or instruction
The revised guidelines were issued on Monday morning.
To be affected
to be changed by a decision that somebody else took
Existing contracts are not affected by the revision.
Pending
waiting for a decision that has not been taken yet
The waiver request is still pending.
As of
starting from that exact date
As of the first of March, the old fare codes are no longer valid.
To notify
to tell somebody officially that something has happened
Clients will be notified by their account manager, not by a system.
In stages
done in separate steps, one after another
The platform will be introduced in stages, country by country.
Mandatory
something that is required, not optional
Attendance at the training session is mandatory.

paras: The quarterly announcement arrives on a Monday and it is written the way these documents are always written. Three points, no names, and a great many sentences in which something happens and nobody appears to have done it.

Point one. The regional office in Bogota has been fully staffed as of last week, and the two remaining positions were filled internally. Point two. The new booking platform will be rolled out in March, in stages, and training sessions are going to be scheduled for every account manager beforehand. Attendance is mandatory. Point three. The corporate fare structure has been revised. Existing contracts are not affected, and clients will be notified by their account manager.

Most of that is written well. When a process matters more than the person behind it, the passive is exactly the right tool: nobody needs to know who schedules the training. But one sentence in point three is different. The corporate fare structure has been revised tells a client that his price may change and refuses to say who decided it or when. The answer, if you ask, is simple: pricing revised it in March and the regional director approved it two weeks ago.

So there is a habit worth building, on both sides. When you read a company email, ask every sentence a single question: who did this? And when you write one, remember that the passive describes a process beautifully and delivers bad news badly. A statement that says a request is pending is fine. A statement that says a request has been refused, with no name attached, is not.
quiz: Why does the text defend the passive in point two?
Because it is more formal and formal is always better.
Because the process matters and nobody needs to know who schedules the training.
Because the writer did not know who was responsible.
What is the problem with "the corporate fare structure has been revised"?
It tells a client his price may change and refuses to say who decided.
What single question does the text tell you to ask of every corporate sentence?
Still waiting for a decision that has not been taken.

tip.title: The Passive Voice
tip.intro: The sentence that puts the action first and the person last -- or nowhere at all. It is the default style of every corporate announcement you receive, and knowing how it is built is half of understanding those emails.
rows: The thing that receives the action becomes the subject. Only be changes tense; the third form never moves.
is operated · was opened · has been approved · will be notified
The person or company appears only if you choose to show them. Most corporate sentences leave it out.
When it is the right choice
When the process matters more than the person, when the agent is obvious, or when naming somebody would be unfair.
"The platform will be rolled out in March."
When it is the wrong choice
Bad news, and anything where the reader is waiting to know who decided. Then it sounds like hiding.

NOT "Your request has been refused."
Say who refused it, and why.
After be comes the third form, not the past: take, took, taken · write, wrote, written.

NOT "The decision was took."
"The decision was taken."
tip.note: A habit worth building when you read a company email: ask every sentence who did this? Half the time the answer is missing, and noticing that is already half of understanding the message.

blanks: Hint: present passive -- is plus the third form of operate
The route is operated by three airlines.
Hint: past passive -- was plus the third form of open
The regional office was opened last September.
Hint: present perfect passive -- has been plus the third form of approve
The proposal has been approved by the director.
Hint: future passive -- will be plus the third form of notify
Clients will be notified before the first of March.
Hint: the third form of take is not took
The decision was taken at headquarters, not here.
Hint: negative present passive -- are not plus the third form of affect
Existing contracts are not affected by the revision.

order.intro: Listen to the summary of the conversation about the quarterly announcement, then put the steps in the correct order.
items: Felipe says the quarterly announcement has been sent to all four countries and asks whether Rosa has read it.
Rosa answers that she has read it twice and that one sentence is not clear.
Felipe asks which sentence, and Rosa quotes the line about the fare structure being revised.
Felipe explains who actually took the decision and why the announcement does not say so.
Rosa says she will call her clients herself instead of letting them read it in a central email.

speech: The new platform will be rolled out in March, in stages.
Existing contracts are not affected by the revision.
The request is still pending, and I will chase it today.
As of the first of March, the old fare codes are no longer valid.
Pricing revised the structure in March, and I am calling you myself.

quiz.intro: You are reading the quarterly announcement and then calling a worried client. Choose the best thing to say.
items: You want to describe the launch of the platform. You say:
The platform will be roll out in March.
The platform will be rolled out in March, in stages.
The platform will roll out in March by the company.
You want to say the decision came from headquarters. You say:
The decision was took at headquarters.
The decision was taken at headquarters, not here.
The decision taken at headquarters, not here.
A client asks whether his contract changes. You say:
Existing contracts are not affected by the revision.
Existing contracts do not affect by the revision.
Existing contracts are not affect by the revision.
You have to tell a colleague that compliance refused his waiver. The better sentence is:
Your waiver request has been refused.
Compliance refused the waiver, because the contract was signed in March.
The waiver was refused, unfortunately.
You want to say the change starts exactly on the first of March. You say:
Since the first of March, the old fare codes will not be valid.
As of the first of March, the old fare codes are no longer valid.
From the first of March, the old fare codes were no longer valid.

think: Take one real change your company announced this year and record the announcement out loud, in about ninety seconds and in three points. Use the passive for the parts that describe a process, and use one active sentence, with a name and a date, for the part where hiding the person would be unfair. Then say the one line you would add if you were calling a client instead of writing to everybody.
survival: The new platform will be rolled out in March, in stages.
Existing contracts are not affected by the revision.
The request is still pending, and I will chase it today.
As of the first of March, the old fare codes are no longer valid.
Pricing revised the structure in March, and I am calling you myself.
